messages:
Sam: Quick kickoff thread for the Acme POC — we need to lock success metrics, auth model, quotas, and a realistic 3-week sprint plan. Proposed: integration -> evals -> tuning/handoff. Anyone see major blockers?

Priya: thanks. can you confirm core flows? generation (chat/summary) + embeddings for semantic search?

Jordan: yep — customer wants realtime meeting-summary generation (streamed) + embeddings for search against their product docs. Typical prompt length small; responses ~20–60 tokens. They expect ~100–200 user requests/sec at peak.

Alex: 200 RPS is a production tier. For initial POC I'd recommend we cap to 30–50 RPS on hosted with autoscale-burst enabled, otherwise Dedicated/reserved capacity will be required.

Sam: noted. pricing question from account: they asked for a rough cost estimate for 200 RPS -> how to ballpark?

Alex: quick calc: assume avg response 40 tokens out, 10 tokens in => 50 tokens total. At hosted rate (example) $0.0005 / 1k tokens => per-request = 50/1000 * $0.0005 = $0.000025. 200 RPS * 3600s * per-request ≈ $18 / hour. This is a rough example — we should provide a tailored quote and point out Dedicated discounts.

Priya: security checklist: they require SOC2, data residency, and KMS for keys. For initial phase they prefer hosted but must have an option to move to Private (VPC + customer KMS) later.

Jordan: they also asked about token retention & logs. We'll need to confirm whether we retain prompts for telemetry by default; customer wants logs retention disabled for PII.

Alex: on auth/SDK: we support API keys for server-server calls. For streaming from client we recommend issuing short-lived session tokens (JWT) via our token minting API on a trusted backend. Example header: Authorization: Bearer <session_jwt>. SDKs (node/python) include helpers for streaming and automatic reconnects.

Alex: snippet for Node streaming (pseudocode):
```
// get ephemeral token from backend
const resp = await fetch('/mint-session');
const token = await resp.text();
const ws = new WebSocket(`wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-2`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
ws.onmessage = (ev) => appendChunk(ev.data);
ws.onclose = (e) => /* retry with backoff */;
```

Sam: do we provide rate-limit headers so their client can backoff gracefully?

Alex: yes — hosted responses include: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. SDK surfaces these and has a default retry strategy: exponential backoff + full jitter. Use "Idempotency-Key" header for retries on generation requests if you need dedup.

Priya: on quotas: for the POC let's propose a soft quota of 50 RPS with configurable bursts to 150 for short tests. Also limit total tokens/day to control cost.

Jordan: success criteria suggestion (we should confirm with Acme):
- Functional: streaming summaries for 95% of calls without errors for 2k sample calls.
- Latency: p95 response-first-byte < 250ms for single-turn short prompts.
- Quality: embedding-based recall >= 0.8 on their 100 curated queries (we'll run eval harness).
- Cost: opportunistic target <$0.02 / user session (we'll define session token counts).
- Ops: integration with their auth flow (ephemeral keys) + no persisted PII in logs.

Sam: timeline proposal:
Week 0 (prep): share SDK examples + security answers; scope finalization.
Week 1: integration and smoke tests (node demo app + basic streaming).
Week 2: run evals (embedding recall, summary quality) + tweak prompt templates.
Week 3: optimize batching/quantization suggestions if needed, handoff + runbook.

QA Bot: smoke test checklist (short):
- basic auth works with ephemeral token
- streaming socket establishes and receives chunks
- headers include rate-limit info
- retry path exercised with simulated 429

Alex: on retries — recommend client-side: max 5 attempts, exponential base 200ms, max backoff 10s, jitter. Server returns Retry-After for long backs off.

Sam: blockers: if they insist on 200 RPS from day 1 and private deployment, procurement lead time for Private is ~4–6 weeks. Call this out in the SOW.

Priya: I'll send the security Q questionnaire answers and a note on data controls by EOD. Also asking Sales to confirm final eval queries list.

Jordan: I'll prepare the embedding eval harness and a 100-query gold set. Need sample size and relevance labels from Acme.

Sam: great. I'll update the POC doc with the KPIs and the week-by-week plan and ping legal/solutions for quote on Dedicated vs Private. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy queued for preview env — build 4721 started (for demo app).

Sam: cool — once preview is up we'll run the Week 1 smoke tests and sync with Acme.
